changes.text: A range volume profile you draw yourself: pick the tool, drag across a stretch of chart, and the volume traded in it is profiled over that span. Built from the same 1-minute bars as the profile on the right, so both agree about where price actually changed hands

Trading sessions on the chart — Asia, London and New York as a futures set, the four classic centres as a forex set, or your own with a name, a time zone and a window. Each session knows the local time of its market, so when the clocks change somewhere the session moves with them instead of drifting an hour off
Every indicator setting now explains itself on hover, in the app's own style rather than a system tooltip. The text sits with the setting it describes, so a new option cannot arrive without one
The minimum size for fair value gaps reads as points as well as percent. Percent keeps its meaning as price moves; points are what you read off your own chart and size a stop in

The VWAP reset — daily or weekly — never actually happened on the chart. Bar times reached the calculation as seconds where a calendar date was expected, which put every bar in 1970 and made both anchors behave like 'whole range'

Inverted fair value gaps were nearly all missing. A retest was counted as using the zone up, when a retest is the reason it is drawn; and a zone that had been broken again was dropped from the stretch of chart where it applied. Both are corrected, and a month of BTC now shows 41 open inversions where it showed 28
The width of a fair value gap box is counted from the bars that formed the gap, so a width of 3 is three candles wide wherever the gap ends up being broken

Fair value gaps on the chart, under Add. A gap is drawn from the three bars that formed it and stays until price fills it — you decide what filling means: first touch, the midpoint, fully crossed, or a close beyond. A minimum size, a window of recent bars and a box width keep the chart as busy or as quiet as you want it

Inverted fair value gaps as a second indicator. A gap that price closes through has failed, and the same prices then read the other way round: failed support becomes resistance. Each zone is drawn from the gap it came from, and a retest leaves it standing — it ends only when price closes back through it

Both zone indicators let you pick the bullish and bearish colour yourself. The palette leads with the candle tones so a zone speaks the same up-is-light, down-is-blue language as the rest of the chart, and every choice works in light and dark

Scrolling back through history no longer stops the chart with an error about bars being out of order. On any timeframe above 1 minute, the boundary between one loaded page and the next fell inside a period, so the same bar arrived twice

The first bar of each page loaded while scrolling back was built from only part of its period, so its open, high, low and close were wrong without anything looking amiss. Pages now start and end on period boundaries

The position tool writes everything inside the block now: target and stop with their price and percentage, the entry on the reward side, and the direction with reward-to-risk against the entry line in the risk zone

The summary box above a position block is gone, along with the risk and reward amounts it showed. The percentages carry the same information and compare across instruments — and the box had been covering the target's percentage
Download years of 1-minute history straight from Binance's public archive — no API key, no account, no subscription. Every file is checksum-verified and stored on your own machine
Charts in seven timeframes, from 1 minute to daily, with older bars loading as you scroll back
Volume profile with point of control, value area and a buy/sell delta. It is always built from 1-minute bars, so the profile does not change just because you switched the chart to 4h
Indicators: moving average, exponential MA, Bollinger Bands, RSI, ATR and VWAP. Oscillators get their own pane instead of sharing a scale with price

Drawing tools — trend line, ray, horizontal and vertical line, rectangle, Fibonacci retracement and a measure tool. Drawings are anchored to time and price, so they stay put through zooming, panning and timeframe changes, and are saved per symbol

Long and short position tools showing entry, stop and target with the risk zone in red and the reward zone in green, plus risk, reward and reward-to-risk. Zone colours and fill opacity are adjustable per drawing

Backtesting engine with market, limit and stop orders, brackets that cancel each other, spread, slippage and commission. Fills are resolved through the 1-minute bars, so a bar that touches both your stop and your target is decided by what actually happened first rather than by a guess
Strategies are plain JavaScript with an onBar hook. They cannot see past the current bar, and an order never fills on the bar that placed it
Light and dark mode, or follow the system — including the native window frame
